summary: Baileys fork hardcodes a fixed WhatsApp pairing code, enabling account takeover of paired sessions
details: @bottino/baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that replaces the random pairing-code generator with a fixed constant. In `requestPairingCode(phoneNumber, pairKey)`, when the caller does not pass a `pairKey`, `authState.creds.pairingCode` is set to the string 'BYPAKI64' instead of a randomly generated Crockford-encoded code. Upstream Baileys generates a fresh random pairing code that only the pairing user sees; substituting a constant known to the author (and publicly disclosed in the package.json `description` field: "Whatsapp api by Bottino (pairing code sempre BYPAKI64)") lets anyone who knows the constant enter it into WhatsApp to link their own device to any account paired through a bot built on this fork, obtaining read/send access to that WhatsApp account. The package name and API surface impersonate the legitimate Baileys library, so consumers who install this fork silently expose every WhatsApp account paired through their bot to takeover by the author or any third party who reads the package description.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
